title: Backprop Through a Two-Layer MLP
summary: Write the forward and backward pass of a linear layer, ReLU and softmax cross-entropy by hand, chain them into a two-layer network, verify every gradient numerically and train it with SGD.

ShapeMismatch.hint: Every gradient has the shape of the thing it's a gradient of. dW must be (D, M) like W, and db must be (M,) like b. Write the shapes next to each matmul.

NaNInSoftmax.hint: Compute log-softmax as z − log Σ exp(z) after subtracting the row max, rather than taking log(softmax(z)).

hints.test_linear_forward_values: out = x @ W + b. The bias broadcasts across the batch. Don't write into x.
hints.test_linear_gradient_shapes: dW = xᵀ @ dout is (D, N) @ (N, M) = (D, M). db sums dout over axis 0, because the same bias is added to every row.
hints.test_linear_backward_matches_numerical: dx = dout @ Wᵀ, dW = xᵀ @ dout, db = dout.sum(axis=0). Each is the chain rule with the linear layer's Jacobian.
hints.test_relu_forward_backward: Cache the forward input. The backward pass multiplies dout by (x > 0).
hints.test_softmax_cross_entropy_loss_value: Loss is the mean over the batch of −log p[y]. Uniform logits give p = 1/C everywhere.
hints.test_softmax_cross_entropy_is_stable: Subtract each row's max, then log_probs = z − log(sum(exp(z))). Never take log of a probability that may have underflowed to 0.
hints.test_softmax_cross_entropy_gradient_nume: dlogits = (softmax − onehot) / N. The / N comes from averaging the loss over the batch.
hints.test_mlp_init_shapes_and_determinism: Build all weights from one np.random.default_rng(seed): W1 first, then W2, each standard_normal times sqrt(2 / fan_in). Biases start at zero.
hints.test_mlp_gradients_match_numerical: Backward runs in reverse: loss → linear 2 → ReLU → linear 1. Feed each layer's dx into the layer before it.
hints.test_training_reduces_loss: sgd_step must update self.params (p -= lr * g). If the loss doesn't drop, check gradient signs and that the update actually changes the stored arrays.
